title: Locking Pretrained Weights via Deep Low-Rank Residual Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2605.10777v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The quality of open-weight language models has dramatically improved in recent years. Sharing weights greatly facilitates model adoption by enabling their use across diverse hardware and software platforms. They also allow for more open research and testing, to the extent that users can use them as checkpoints, fine-tune them according to their needs, and potentially redistribute them. In some cases, however, concerns on modifying these weights towards unauthorized uses may outweigh the pros of giving users such freedom. Defending against such adaptation is non-trivial: since an adaptive attacker can observe all weights and architectures by definition, they can reverse simple structural defenses, and use optimization to defeat the simplest locking mechanisms. translated_abstract: arXiv:2605.10777v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：近年来，开放权重语言模型的质量得到了显著提升。共享权重使模型能够在多样化的硬件和软件平台上使用，极大地促进了模型的采用。开放权重还支持更开放的研究和测试，用户可以将其作为检查点，根据自身需求进行微调，甚至可能重新分发。然而，在某些情况下，对权重进行修改以用于未经授权用途的担忧可能超过给予用户这种自由的好处。防御此类适应性攻击并非易事：由于适应性攻击者按定义可以观察所有权重和架构，他们可以逆转简单的结构性防御，并通过优化手段击败最简单的锁定机制。在这项工作中，我们利用自动微分在推理与训练之间的不对称性作为一种全新的防御轴。我们提出了DLR-Lock方法，其中模型提供者（摘要内容在此处截断）
tldr: 提出DLR-Lock方法，利用自动微分在推理与训练之间的不对称性，通过深度低秩残差蒸馏锁定预训练权重，防止适应性攻击者对开放权重模型进行未经授权的微调和滥用。
en_tdlr: DLR-Lock exploits the inference-training asymmetry of automatic differentiation and deep low-rank residual distillation to lock pretrained weights, preventing adaptive attackers from fine-tuning open-weight models for unauthorized uses.
